recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source edit is recommended because the original compatibility rule is present in active source, and the wording difference is explained by the later approved FHIR-13089 refinement.
issue_request: FHIR-3730 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core FHIR-I change request asking how clients and servers should handle optional, required, and later-added operation parameters. Its accepted resolution was to document that once operation definitions become stable/normative, incompatible operation signature changes should be represented by new operation variants rather than changing the existing signature.
initial_application: The issue was historically applied by SVN-derived git commit e2c9447cca757714ea04d871e5355a3943144692, '#3730 note on operation compatibility', with git-svn-id build@5035 matching the Jira comment. That commit updated source/compatibility.html to say that additional optional parameters may be introduced, but operation signatures cannot change and additional operation variants will be defined.
additional_context: source/compatibility.html was later reorganized into the current active version-management page, source/versions.html. Later Published issue FHIR-13089 explicitly requested replacing the original 'Operation signatures cannot change; instead...' wording with the current source/versions.html wording about defining new operations and potentially deprecating old ones; FHIR-13089 already has an Issue-Reconcile-Key commit on the combined branch. Later Published issue FHIR-38034 added derived OperationDefinition guidance that is consistent with this rule and is also already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/versions.html states that compatibility rules apply once core or HL7 International IG artifacts become normative, and its Operations row already says new operations may be defined, operations and existing parameters will not be removed or renamed, parameter type and lower cardinality will not change, upper cardinality may only be widened from 1 to *, additional optional parameters may be introduced, and incompatible operation changes will be handled by defining new operations and potentially deprecating old operations.
